p: מַה שֶּׁנּוֹהֲגִין לֶאֱכוֹל תַּפּוּחַ מָתוֹק בִּדְבַשׁ
As for the custom to eat a sweet apple in honey
and to ask "that You renew for us
why did they choose specifically an apple
(אִדְּרָא נָשֹׂא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קלג, ב)
פָּסִיק שַׂעֲרָא וְאִתְחֲזְיָין תְּרֵין תַּפּוּחִין וְכוּלֵּי
"The hair breaks off, and two apples are revealed ...."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כז, א)
This follows what they said (Bereishis Rabbah 27:1):
"Great is the power of the Neviim,
who liken the form to its Maker";
וְכֵן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי גַּם כֵּן
and so too Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai
מְתָאֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל בְּצוּרַת אָדָם
describes Hashem Yisbarach, as it were, in the form of a man,
that beneath the hairs of the beard
"'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest ...':
בְּאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים (מִשְׁלֵי טז, טו)
'In the light of the King's face is life' (Mishlei 16:15);
and we have learned: from these apples
life goes forth to the world ...;
כְּתִיב (בַּמִּדְבָּר ו, כה) יָאֵר ה׳ פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וְכוּלֵּי
it is written (Bamidbar 6:25): 'May Hashem shine His face upon you ...' —
And it is written "and be gracious to you": He will grant you favor.
And favor implies even though one is not deserving,
לֹא שֶׁהָיָה כְּדַאי אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּצָא חֵן
"Not that he was worthy, but that he found favor."
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּיקֵּשׁ
Likewise Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, asked
(Shemos 33:16): "For how then will it be known
that I have found favor in Your eyes ...";
for he did not want to make it depend on his deeds,
to be granted an unearned gift
even if he is not worthy.
כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ מָצָא חֵן בַּמִּדְבָּר וְגוֹמֵר
"Thus says Hashem: They found favor in the wilderness ...";
שֶׁאַף שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג עַל הַדּוֹר הַהוּא
for although there was an accusation against that generation
at the Exodus from Egypt and at the splitting of the Sea —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כא, ז וְעוֹד)
as they said (Shemos Rabbah 21:7 and elsewhere) —
nevertheless the generation of the wilderness found
as stated in the holy Zohar
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צב, א וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
therefore on Rosh Hashanah we eat an apple
to arouse above the light of the King's face
from those two apples, as mentioned above;
and through the shining of the face
there will be "and be gracious to you,"
that we merit an unearned gift
For if it were by way of judgment,
מִי יוּכַל לוֹמַר זִכִּיתִי לִבִּי (מִשְׁלֵי כ, ט)
who could say, "I have purified my heart" (Mishlei 20:9)?
And there are accusations against this;
can we ask for an unearned gift.
וַיְהִי אוֹר דָּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְכוּלֵּי
"'And there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah ..." —
on Rosh Hashanah there already is
existence and permanence to the shining of the King's face;
then is the time to ask for the light,
that He shine His face upon us,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִזְכֶּה לִמְצִיאַת חֵן
and through this we will merit finding favor.
אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא הֶאָרַת פָּנֶיךָ
"We have nothing but the shining of Your face;
save me and we shall be saved";
for through the shining of the face
נִזְכֶּה לִישׁוּעָה עַל יְדֵי מַתְּנַת חִנָּם
we will merit salvation as an unearned gift.
"Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah;
Hashem, in the light of Your face they will walk";
שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה עַל יְדֵי הַתְּקִיעוֹת שׁוֹפָר
for on Rosh Hashanah, through the shofar blasts,
we also merit the shining of the face.
to arouse the light of the King's face,
and we ask "that You renew for us a good year" —
meaning the light that is good
for the first "good" in the Torah
נֶאֱמַר וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
is said in: "And Elokim saw the light, that it was good,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית
and afterwards it is said of all the work of Creation,
בְּכָל יוֹם וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב
on each day: "And Elokim saw that it was good";
that in all the work of Creation
יֵשׁ בְּחִינַת הָאוֹר שֶׁנִּקְרָא כִּי טוֹב
there is the aspect of the light called "that it was good."
וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל הַשָּׁנָה
And Rosh Hashanah is the head of the year,
regarding why it is called Rosh Chodesh
and not "the first of the month":
that it is the head of the month,
therefore one can merit on Rosh Hashanah
that the whole year be good,
that we merit in it the light that is good.
In the Gemara (Shabbos 88a) there is expounded
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest" regarding Yisrael,
who are likened to an apple:
מַה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו
"Just as with this apple its fruit comes before its leaves,
so too Yisrael put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"
We have already noted a difficulty:
"Its clusters — these are the talmidei chachamim;
עָלִין שֶׁבָּהּ אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵּי
its leaves — these are the amei ha'aretz ...;
for were it not for the leaves,
According to this, the men of deeds
and the talmidei chachamim are the fruits;
וְכָאן אָמְרוּ עַל שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע
yet here they said, of putting "we will do" before "we will hear,"
that it is like an apple whose fruit comes before its leaves,
making the fruit stand for "we will do."
But the "we will do and we will hear" that they said —
that the doing come before the hearing —
in line with what they said (Sanhedrin 99b):
"as though he had made the words of Torah."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּפֶסַח שֵׁנִי
It is like what we find with Pesach Sheni,
שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
where Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, said to them
what Hashem will command concerning you";
and we said that "stand" means in prayer,
that they cried from the depth of their heart,
אַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ רְאוּיִם לְקָרְבַּן פֶּסַח
though they were not fit for the korban Pesach,
with this outcry before Hashem Yisbarach,
"I will hear what Hashem will command concerning you"
and in line with what they said (Sanhedrin 8a):
but the daughters of Tzelafchad merited,
and it was written through them."
And this is why they said "we will do" first:
we will make words of Torah;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּאִיר ה׳ לֵידַע הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
that is, that Hashem will give us light to know the words of Torah
and the deed that we are to do,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as we find with Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
שֶׁקִּייֵּם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה
who kept the entire Torah before it was given
and from where did he learn the Torah?
Rather, Hashem Yisbarach shone light into his heart,
and he knew on his own all the words of Torah,
And this is what they said (ibid. 2:3):
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham";
for he was the first to merit the light.
And this is why they said that they are likened to an apple,
since they put "we will do" before "we will hear":
we will merit the light of Torah;
and this is "its fruit comes before its leaves":
come before the deed and before hearing in order to do.
וּכְתִיב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ג) בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי
And it is written (Shir HaShirim 2:3): "In His shade I delighted and sat,
and His fruit is sweet to my palate";
הַיְינוּ בְּצִלּוֹ שֶׁהוּא אוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים
that is, "in His shade," which is the light of the King's face that is life,
"and His fruit is sweet to my palate,"
"And the light is sweet, and it is good ...."
And this is why we say "a good and sweet year":
שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה בְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה לְהָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
that we merit all year the light that is good;
and "sweet," that we feel taste in words of Torah,
And we find, regarding the four who entered the Pardes
"Ben Zoma ... of him the verse says
(מִשְׁלֵי כה, טז) דְּבַשׁ מָצָאתָ אֱכוֹל דַּיֶּיךָּ
(Mishlei 25:16): 'Have you found honey? Eat what suffices you,
lest you be sated with it and vomit it'";
for at times one can receive
more than is fitting for him in the secrets of the Torah,
"'Honey and milk are under your tongue' —
And about this they said "and sweet":
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָאִיר לָנוּ בְּהֶאָרַת פָּנִים
that Hashem Yisbarach shine upon us with the shining of His face
לְקַבֵּל רַק דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָרְאוּיִם לָנוּ
to receive only words of Torah fitting for us,
that there be "and the light is sweet,"
that the words of Torah shine in the heart,
And the essence of words of Torah is the light,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, ד)
when Yisrael heard "I am Hashem your God,"
"the learning of Torah was implanted in their heart ...."
אַף שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמְעוּ רַק מַאֲמַר אָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
Although they heard only the utterance "I am Hashem your God,"
once it shone in their heart in truth
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בַּעַל הַכּוֹחוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם
that Hashem Yisbarach is the Master of their powers —
this is the light of the King's face;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְכָל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and through this they merited all the words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
just as Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom, merited
and understood with his own mind
לְקַיֵּים כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה
to keep all the words of Torah before it was given.
And to this the apple points,
whose fruit comes before its leaves:
that there be a "making" of words of Torah.
So too we find that it is written (Nechemiah 8:10):
"Eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks ...,
for the day is holy to our Lord."
וְהוּא דְּיוֹם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִקְרָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים
This is because the day of Rosh Hashanah is called in the Tikkunim
there remains the resh — Rosh Hashanah";
וְהוּא דְּחַג הַזֶּה הוּא נֶגֶד יִצְחָק
That is, this festival corresponds to Yitzchak
and of him we find that he said to Esav
that there was holiness in Esav,
אֲבָל עִיקַּר הַמַּטְעַמִּים הָיוּ עֲבוּר יַעֲקֹב
but the delicacies were really for Yaakov,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג ק, א)
as stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 100a):
And this is what is said (Tehillim 89:16):
"Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah,"
and it is stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 29:4):
וְכִי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין יוֹדְעִין לְהָרִיעַ
"Do the nations of the world not know how to sound the teruah?
how to win over their Creator with the teruah."
And on this the verse concludes:
"Hashem, in the light of Your face they will walk";
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְהָאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ
for through this they merit the light of the King's face,
"For the day is holy to our Lord":
שֶׁאֵין אוֹכְלִים רַק לִכְבוֹד קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם
we eat only in honor of the holiness of the day;
and this is "and drink sweet drinks":
that it be as it says, "And the light is sweet,"
that we feel a taste of sweetness in words of Torah
and receive the light in measure, as is fitting,
that it be "eat what suffices you," as mentioned above.
For this reason we eat a sweet apple in honey:
that through the arousal from below
the light of the King's face that is life,
so that the whole year be
a good and sweet year, as stated.
